sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: Parsley is a cultivated biennial herb, usually 30–100 cm tall. It is widely grown and probably originated in the Mediterranean region.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The basal leaves are divided several times and may be flat or curly. Small yellow-green flowers grow in compound umbels. The dry fruits are about 2–4 × 1.5–3 mm.

sections.title: Culinary use
sections.text: The leaves and stems are used as a seasoning. Some tuberous varieties are grown for their root, but this use does not apply to every cultivar.
